craw-0005.text: Today he is there to trip you up. And he will torture you tomorrow. Yet he is also there to ease the pain, when you are lost in grief and sorrow.

craw-0006.text: Come up and let us go. Go down and here we stay.

craw-0008.text: I'm very tempting, so its said, I have a shiny coat of red, and my flesh is white beneath. I smell so sweet, taste good to eat, and help to guard your teeth.

craw-0009.text: I fly through the air on small feathered wings, seeking out life and destroying all things.

craw-0010.text: I have many feathers to help me fly. I have a body and head, but I'm not alive. It is your strength which determines how far I go. You can hold me in your hand, but I'm never thrown.

craw-0011.text: I can be moved. I can be rolled. But nothing will I hold. I'm red and I'm blue, and I can be other colors too. Having no head, though similar in shape. I have no eyes - yet move all over the place.

craw-0012.text: A time when they're green. A time when they're brown. But both of these times, cause me to frown. But just in between, for a very short while. They're perfect and yellow. And cause me to smile.

craw-0013.text: My first is in blood and also in battle. My second is in acorn, oak, and apple. My third and fourth are both the same. In the center of sorrow and twice in refrain. My fifth starts eternity ending here. My last is the first of last, Oh Dear.

craw-0014.text: I sleep by day, I fly by night. I have no feathers to aid my flight.

craw-0015.text: When I’m metal or wood, I help you get home. When I’m flesh and I’m blood, In the darkness I roam.

craw-0016.text: I am the yellow hem of the sea's blue skirt.

craw-0017.text: In the night a mountain, in the morning a meadow.

craw-0021.text: Round as a button, deep as a well. If you want me to talk, you must first pull my tail.

craw-0022.text: You heart it speak, for it has a hard tongue. But it cannot breathe, for it has not a lung.

craw-0023.text: I am a fire's best friend. When fat, my body fills with wind. When pushed to thin, through my nose I blow. Then you can watch the embers glow.

craw-0024.text: You get many of me, but never enough. After the last one, your life soon will snuff. You may have one of me but one day a year, When the last one is gone, your life disappears.

craw-0025.text: I am seen in the water. If seen in the sky, I am in the rainbow, a jay's feather, and lapis lazuli.

craw-0026.text: My life is often a volume of grief, your help is needed to turn a new leaf. Stiff is my spine and my body is pale. But I'm always ready to tell a tale.

craw-0027.text: Turns us on our backs, and open up our stomachs. You will be the wisest of men though at start a lummox.

craw-0028.text: I heard of a wonder, of words moth-eaten. That is a strange thing, I thought, weird. That a man's song be swallowed by a worm. His blinded sentences, his bedside stand-by rustled in the night - and the robber-guest. Not one wit the wiser. For the words he had mumbled.

craw-0030.text: I have a neck but no head. I have a body but no arm. I have a bottom but no leg.

craw-0031.text: As light as a feather, but you can’t hold it for ten minutes.

craw-0032.text: Hard to catch, easy to hold. Can't be seen, unless it's cold.

craw-0033.text: I am free for the taking. Through all of your life, though given but once at birth. I am less than nothing in weight, but will fell the strongest of you if held.

craw-0034.text: I'm light as a feather, yet the strongest man can't hold me for more than 5 minutes.

craw-0035.text: To cross the water I'm the way, for water I'm above. I touch it not and, truth to say, I neither swim nor move.

craw-0036.text: All about the house, with his lady he dances, yet he always works, and never romances.

craw-0037.text: I have a hundred legs, but cannot stand. I have a long neck, but no head. I cannot see. I'm neat and tidy as can be.

craw-0038.text: A muttered rumble was heard from the pen, and I, in my walking stopped to look in. What was this I saw? A massive beast, hoofed, and jawed. With spikes upon its mighty brow, I watched as he struck the turf and prowled. And yet for all of his magnificence, he couldn't get out of that wooden fence.

craw-0039.text: What lies in a tunnel of darkness. That can only attack when pulled back?

craw-0040.text: Flat as a leaf, round as a ring. Has two eyes, can't see a thing.

craw-0041.text: No matter how little or how much you use me, you change me every month.

craw-0042.text: I have one eye. See near and far. I hold the moments you treasure and the things that make you weep.

craw-0044.text: My life can be measured in hours. I serve by being devoured. Thin, I am quick. Fat, I am slow. Wind is my foe.

craw-0045.text: What has 13 hearts but none beat?

craw-0046.text: What kind of pet always stays on the floor?

craw-0047.text: Halo of water, tongue of wood. Skin of stone, long I've stood. My fingers short reach to the sky. Inside my heart men live and die.

craw-0048.text: Stealthy as a shadow in the dead of night, cunning but affectionate if given a bite. Never owned but often loved. At my sport considered cruel, but that's because you never know me at all.

craw-0049.text: Though desert men once called me God, today men call me mad. For I wag my tail when I am angry. And growl when I am glad.

craw-0050.text: I'm not really more than holes tied to more holes. I'm strong as good steel, though not as stiff as a pole.

craw-0051.text: I have legs but walk not, a strong back but work not. Two good arms but reach not. A seat but sit and tarry not.

craw-0052.text: What's black when you get it, red when you use it, and white when you're all through with it?

craw-0053.text: Not born, but from a Mother's body drawn. I hang until half of me is gone. I sleep in a cave until I grow old. Then valued for my hardened gold.

craw-0054.text: I wear a red robe, with staff in hand, and a stone in my throat.

craw-0057.text: I have a face, yet no senses. But I don't really care, because time is of the essence.

craw-0058.text: This thing runs but cannot walk, sometimes sings but never talks. Lacks arms, has hands; lacks a head but has a face.

craw-0059.text: I fly, yet I have no wings. I cry, yet I have no eyes. Darkness follows me. Lower light I never see.

craw-0060.text: Black we are and much admired. Many seek us if they are tired. We tire the horse, and comfort man, and turn White when we've fulfilled your plan.

craw-0065.text: I am two-faced but bear only one. I have no legs but travel widely. Men spill much blood over me. Kings leave their imprint on me. I have greatest power when given away, yet lust for me keeps me locked away.

craw-0066.text: What can you catch but not throw?

craw-0067.text: Metal or bone I may be, many teeth I have and always bared. Yet my bite harms no one. And ladies delight in my touch.

craw-0068.text: I am so simple that I can only point. Yet I guide men all over the world.

craw-0073.text: Some try to hide, some try to cheat. But time will show, we always will meet. Try as you might, to guess my name. I promise you'll know, when you I do claim.

craw-0079.text: What has six faces and twenty-one eyes?

craw-0081.text: Hands she has but does not hold. Teeth she has but does not bite. Feet she has but they are cold. Eyes she has but without sight.

craw-0084.text: My first is in window but not in pane. My second's in road but not in lane. My third is in oval but not in round. My fourth is in hearing but not in sound. My whole is known as a sign of peace. And from noah's ark won quick release.

craw-0085.text: A word I know, six letters it contains. Subtract just one and twelve remains.

craw-0086.text: This is in a realm of true and in a realm false, but you experience me as you turn and toss.

craw-0087.text: Although my cow is dead, I still beat her What a racket she makes.

craw-0088.text: People are hired to get rid of me. I'm often hiding under your bed. In time I'll always return you see. Bite me and you're surely dead.

craw-0089.text: I am the third from a sparkle bright, I thrive throughout the day and night. Deep in the path of a cows white drink. I've had thousands of millions of years to think. But one of my creatures is killing me. And so the question I ask to thee, is
